strings.name: Viswanathan Anand
strings.role: Chess player and FIDE Deputy President
strings.summary: Viswanathan Anand became India’s first chess grandmaster and won five world championship events or matches. Renowned for fast calculation and adaptability across formats, he helped broaden Indian participation and talent development. FIDE Deputy President since 2022, he served as interim president from July to September 2026. Following September’s election, he remained Deputy President under new president Timur Turlov.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through November 16, 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Multiple world championships helped develop Indian chess talent and public participation.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f1.value: Mayiladuthurai, Tamil Nadu, India; raised in Chennai.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Five world championships
strings.highlights.h1.text: Won the FIDE title in 2000, became undisputed champion in 2007 and defended the title in 2008, 2010 and 2012.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education and early training
strings.facts.f2.value: Learned chess from his mother, attended Don Bosco school in Chennai and earned a commerce degree from Loyola College.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Building Indian chess
strings.highlights.h2.text: India’s first grandmaster and world champion helped raise the sport’s profile and supported younger players’ development.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Continued as Deputy President
strings.timeline.t1.text: The Samarkand assembly elected Timur Turlov president and Anand deputy, ending Anand’s interim presidency.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Assumed interim presidential duties
strings.timeline.t2.text: After Dvorkovich suspended his duties following EU sanctions, Anand assumed the presidency under FIDE’s charter.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Joined FIDE leadership
strings.timeline.t3.text: Was elected Deputy President, bringing a player’s experience to international competition and governance.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Another world rapid title
strings.timeline.t4.text: Won the World Rapid Championship in Riyadh, demonstrating enduring strength at faster time controls.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Lost the classical world title
strings.timeline.t5.text: Lost the Chennai match to Carlsen, ending his undisputed reign begun in 2007; won the Candidates the following year for another challenge.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Undisputed world champion
strings.timeline.t6.text: Won the Mexico City championship tournament and subsequently defended in matches in 2008, 2010 and 2012.
strings.timeline.t7.title: First world title
strings.timeline.t7.text: Won FIDE’s knockout world championship, becoming India’s first world champion.
strings.timeline.t8.title: India’s first grandmaster
strings.timeline.t8.text: Earned the grandmaster title after winning the 1987 World Junior Championship, establishing his international standing.
